fix_assessment.rationale: A repository change is applicable: the diagnostic stack names a specific search method with unsafe null assumptions. The plan is intentionally yellow because the issue's screenshot and query are not connected conclusively.

proposed_fixes.title: Make Window Walker fuzzy search tolerate invalid window snapshots
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A window or its Process data can be null or incomplete in the snapshot consumed by FuzzySearchOpenWindows, but the method dereferences window.Title and window.Process.Name without a guard; that can abort query processing.
plan: In src/modules/launcher/Plugins/Microsoft.Plugin.WindowWalker/Components/SearchController.cs, inspect the snapshot contract and identify whether null Window entries or null Process values are possible during window churn.
Guard invalid entries and missing process metadata in FuzzySearchOpenWindows, preserving title matching when available and treating missing process names as a non-match instead of throwing.
Add focused tests around null/incomplete snapshot entries and retain the existing empty-title filtering semantics.
Reproduce the reporter's query on the latest stable build to determine whether the visible error disappears; do not treat the defensive change as proof of the screenshot cause without that check.
verification: Run the Window Walker/PowerToys Run unit tests covering SearchController and add a null/incomplete-window case if the existing test project exposes this seam.
Reproduce the original screenshot sequence with the exact query and confirm Run remains responsive and renders results.
Repeat after updating from 0.100.2 to the latest stable release to separate an already-fixed version issue from a current regression.

confidence.rationale: The diagnostic method and unsafe dereferences match a credible crash path, but the query, screenshot state, and current-version behavior are unconfirmed.

design.root_cause: Likely null or incomplete Window data during fuzzy search causes SearchController.FuzzySearchOpenWindows to dereference unavailable title/process metadata.
evidence: Diagnostic stack identifies FuzzySearchOpenWindows during UpdateSearchText.
Current source dereferences window.Title and window.Process.Name without validation.
The exact query and screenshot connection remain unconfirmed.

affected_files.purpose: Filters and scores open-window snapshots for PowerToys Run.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Every snapshot entry is assumed to have a title and Process.Name.
implementation_steps.change: Skip null entries, require a usable title, and make process-name matching optional when process metadata is unavailable.
implementation_steps.code_block: foreach (var window in openWindows ?? Enumerable.Empty<Window>()) { if (window is null || string.IsNullOrEmpty(window.Title)) continue; var processName = window.Process?.Name; var titleMatch = ...; var processMatch = string.IsNullOrEmpty(processName) ? EmptyMatch : ...; ... }
edge_cases: Do not hide valid windows solely because Process is unavailable.
Keep snapshot processing deterministic and avoid a broad catch that hides unrelated defects.
tests: Add focused cases for null entries, missing Process, empty title, and normal title/process matches.

verify: Run the existing targeted Window Walker/PowerToys Run tests after locating the project command.
Repeat the exact query and screenshot sequence on the latest stable build.
Confirm Run stays responsive and that normal title/process fuzzy matching is unchanged.
risks: A null guard can hide a lifecycle defect if logging is omitted.
Title-only results may change ranking when process metadata is absent.
alternatives: Fix only the shortcut repository duplicate error: rejected because the diagnostic stack names Window Walker fuzzy search.
Add a broad exception handler: rejected because it would conceal malformed snapshot bugs and make results silently incomplete.
